title: Stare Settings — look and feel
brief: Reorganise the macOS Settings window now that it holds 31 preferences: group the sidebar into a natural map, use space better, and keep every live preview in view while the user edits it (today the pointer preview is the last card of a long scrolling pane, so the user cannot see what they are changing).

artboards.title: 01 · Pinned preview rail
artboards.tradeoff: The preview never scrolls and never leaves the viewport, at the cost of a permanent 266 pt column that panes without a preview cannot use. Bar pane reuses the rail with the vertical bar preview.

artboards.title: 02 · Stage-first band
artboards.tradeoff: Preview pinned as a full-width stage above the controls, so the wide bar preview and the square pointer tiles both fit, and the controls below use two columns. Costs ~200 pt of vertical space on every previewable pane; rows get ~350 pt each instead of full width.

artboards.title: 03 · Promoted preview, compact column
artboards.tradeoff: Cheapest and least structural: today's cards, one capped 620 pt column, preview moved directly under the first group. It is visible on open, but it still scrolls away on the long panes.
